name: Peugh v. United States
summary: The Supreme Court held that sentencing a defendant under guidelines harsher than those in effect at the time of the offense violates the Ex Post Facto Clause, recognizing that guidelines retain substantial practical force even though they are technically advisory.
significance: Peugh recognized that the Sentencing Guidelines exert a powerful influence over actual sentences even after Booker, underscoring why the question of deference to commentary has significant practical consequences for defendants.
